A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

interface engineering of a 2D topological superconductivity in the Fe/Re system is achieved via an atomically thin FeO layer, which is the first step toward the realization of a topological quantum computer based on Majorana fermions.
the interface engineering of the Fe-Re hybrid system leads to the realization of a topological superconducing state with Majorana edge modes.

the topological superconductivity in the Fe/Re(0001)-oxide hybrid system can be tuned by controlling the interface properties, and the topological superconductive state is stabilized by a strong proximity effect between Fe and the Re(0001) surface, which can be further enhanced by the presence of an atomically thin ReO _{2} layer at the Fe/Re interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interplay of magnetism and superconductivity can be exploited to create and control Majorana edge states at the atomic scale, paving the way for the development of topological quantum devices.

the topological phase is realized by the combination of the magnetic proximity effect and a strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling at the interface, which are both crucial ingredients for the realization of a topological superconductive state.

the topological properties of the Fe/ Re hybrid system are highly sensitive to atomic-scale structural and chemical details of the interface, which opens new avenues for the realization of Majorana edge states.
